venture.description: A gourmet, island-inspired applesauce targeted at adults, featuring exotic flavors and baked apple wedges.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Presents Sanaia, an adult applesauce with exotic flavors and baked wedges, comparing the market opportunity to the yogurt industry.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Hands out samples of the different applesauce flavors to the panel.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Asks if the product is currently in the market or brand new.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Explains they launched in July and did a six-month test market direct to consumer.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Asks what the current sales figures are.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: States they achieved $40,000 in sales during the six-month test pilot.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Asks if people buy it for the flavor or as a health food.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Explains people seek plant-based options, move away from dairy, and vegans use it for baking.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Asks how the product is sold and what its cost is.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Details the upcoming Amazon Prime launch of a 4-pack, stating the cost to make and retail price per jar.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Calculates and verifies the total retail price and cost for the 4-pack.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Confirms his calculation is correct.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Challenges the price, asking if it is not expensive for applesauce.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Argues they are not comparing to Mott's, citing the Chobani yogurt transformation, and mentions $35M in projected revenue from a trade show.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Expresses disbelief at the $35 million projected revenue claim.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Offers to explain how she arrived at the number.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Asks her to explain who said what regarding the projection.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Lists major retailers like Starbucks, Whole Foods, and Kroger who showed interest.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Asks if she received a firm order from anyone.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Admits they have not received firm orders, only confirmed interest.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Points out that buyers noted no one else is doing this and that it belongs in the refrigerated section.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Asks if she has a test running with Whole Foods.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Confirms they are in Whole Foods in Harlem.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Clarifies if it is just one store.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Confirms it is only one store.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Presses her on how she calculated the 35 million dollar figure.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Explains the projection is based on the number of buyers who approached them.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Asks again if she received a firm order from anybody.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Reiterates they have not received firm orders, only confirmed interest.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Shows pictures of the new yogurt cup packaging format.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Asks if they can see the new packaging format.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Hands out the new plastic cup packaging to the investors.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Asks about her professional background.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: States she is the Global Head of HR for a large publishing company.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Asks which publishing company she works for.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Names News Corp and mentions she has been there for six years.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Asks if she is running this business on the side.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Confirms she is doing it on the side but emphasizes her experience building high-performance teams.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Asks if she plans to go full-time into the business.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Explains it doesn't make sense to go full-time yet, noting she hired a full-time COO.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Asks if she has raised a lot of money, observing it sounds expensive.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: States she has been self-funding it so far, investing $250,000.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Compliments her for getting very far on $250,000.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Asks what her plan is for the glass jar product versus the plastic cup.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: States the glass jars will be available on Amazon Prime in two weeks.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Expresses strong disapproval of the plan to sell glass jars on Amazon.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Reiterates that she is launching the glass jars in two weeks.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Points out that the shipping cost for heavy glass jars will be enormous.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Defends the choice by stating they make close to 50% margins on the glass jars.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Asks what the cost of the plastic cup will be.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: States the plastic cup costs 63 cents to make.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Asks what the selling price of the plastic cup will be.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Provides the wholesale and retail prices for the plastic cup.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Declares it the most expensive applesauce ever sold in America.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Argues that a person who buys Mott's is not their target consumer.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Acknowledges her point but implies it's still a difficult path.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Reiterates their goal to create a new category.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Argues it will be hard to sell as an unestablished brand and questions complicating it with glass packaging.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Simply states that they started with glass packaging.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Explains she is not an applesauce fan and questions the adult market demand, deciding to drop out.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Respectfully accepts her decision.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Praises her presentation skills and performance up until the trade show discussion.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Expresses doubt due to her confusing interest with actual orders and decides to exit.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Thanks him for his feedback.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Compliments the product and states the pricing is not out of line.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Calls her a dreamer, questions her projections, and states any offer she would make would be insulting.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Asks what valuation would prompt an offer, stating she wouldn't be insulted.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Offers the requested amount for a very large equity stake.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Repeats her offer after the commercial break.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Jokes with the panel about not being insulted by the offer.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Appreciates her response.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Formally declines the offer.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Exits following the rejection of her offer.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Criticizes her for not working on the business full-time, questioning her commitment.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Explains she is the breadwinner and quitting her job isn't an option.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Acknowledges that quitting a job isn't an option for everyone.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: States he prefers to invest in full-time entrepreneurs and exits.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Asks how much cash she has in the bank.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: States she has set aside close to $500,000 for the business.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Clarifies the breakdown of her invested and saved funds.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Confirms his understanding of her finances.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Expresses doubt that she is a true entrepreneur despite her strong presence.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Defends her entrepreneurial drive, highlighting her financial risks and round-the-clock work.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Points out again that she is still employed elsewhere.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Confirms she does have another job.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Argues that part-time implies a lack of full dedication.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Agrees with the point about part-time work.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Explains she mitigated her part-time status by putting a dedicated team in place, as she cannot afford to quit.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Questions why investors should believe in her if she is not fully committed.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Pushes back, noting she started a previous company while having heavy financial obligations and had no choice.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Notices her emotion and asks why she is tearing up.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Explains the emotional weight of providing for many people financially and doing this for herself.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Validates her responsibility, agreeing she shouldn't squander commitments if she didn't believe in the business.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Asks specifically who relies on her financially.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Lists her parents and siblings as dependents.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Supports her decision to keep her job and take care of her family while building the business.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Calls her impressive and states his team can fill in the missing pieces for her business.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Makes an offer for the requested amount at a higher equity stake.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Accepts the offer made by the investor.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Confirms the deal.

Feels doubt because she confused trade show interest with actual firm orders.
Thinks projections are unbelievable, requires huge equity to justify the risk.
Rejects the offer, finding the required equity stake unacceptable.
Exits immediately after her offer is rejected.
Prefers to invest in an entrepreneur who works on the business full-time.
Impressed by her drive; believes his team can provide the missing operational pieces.
Comfortable with the terms and accepts the offer.
